values.note: 48 back-in sites (002-050; no 001 or 027), catalogued at 20-45 ft; all but 012 and 025 (20 ft) take 23 ft or more. Gravel or dirt spurs; every vehicle must fit on the spur (no parking on the grass). One RV and two tents, or two tents, per site.

sites.source: recreation.gov catalog 232017 (48 STANDARD NONELECTRIC sites; Max Vehicle Length 20-45; Driveway Entry Back-In except 024, which gives none) + recreation.gov 232017 ('Parking spurs are gravel or dirt'; 'all vehicles must fit in the parking spur. Please no parking on the grass.'; '2 tent maximum per site. Or 1 RV and 2 tents.'), read 2026-10-28

values.note: No water in 2025 or 2026 - bring your own, including enough to drown a campfire; the RV dump stations at Printer Boy and White Star are also closed. Trash collection, picnic tables, fire rings; some accessible sites; firewood sold at the host site.

facilities.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc/recreation/baby-doe-campground ('Potable water is not available at this site. Water will not be available in this campground in 2025.'; 'Vault toilets are located throughout the campground.') + recreation.gov 232017 notice ('Water will NOT be available in this campground in 2026. ... the RV Dump Stations at both Printer Boy & White Star Campgrounds will remain closed this season.'; amenities: Accessible Vault Toilets, Trash Collection, Picnic Tables, Campfire Rings), read 2026-10-28

values.note: May to September; opening and closing dates are weather dependent, and water, trash or a host may be missing early and late in the season.

season.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc/recreation/baby-doe-campground ('Seasons of Use: May to September. Opening and closing dates are weather dependent. Services such as water, trash or a host may not be available during early and late season.'), read 2026-10-28

values.note: Book on recreation.gov or 877-444-6777 at least four days ahead (2026 season May 22 - Sep 19; 2027 from May 28). Reservations must cover both Friday and Saturday nights on weekends and three nights on holiday weekends; walk-ups are exempt from the minimum. First-come sites must be occupied the first night; pay at the self-service fee tube (cash, check or money order).

booking.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc/recreation/baby-doe-campground ('Call 877-444-6777 or visit recreation.gov at least four days in advance. A minimum stay on Friday and Saturday night is required on weekends. A three-night minimum stay is required on holiday weekends. Walk-ups are exempt from the nightly minimum.'; 'First-come, first-served sites must be occupied the first night.') + recreation.gov 232017 (rules: reservationCutOff 4; rates: Peak Season 2026-05-22 to 09-06 and 09-07 to 09-19, 2027 from 05-28), read 2026-10-28

values.note: $29 a site per night; $33 on sites 4-11, 13 and 14. Two vehicles and one RV included (an RV and its tow vehicle arriving together count as one); $11 a night for each extra vehicle, boat and ATV trailers included.

fees.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc/recreation/baby-doe-campground ('Single Site: $29- $33 per night'; '$33 fee for overnight camping on sites 4-11, 13 and 14.'; '$11 fee for a third vehicle.') + recreation.gov 232017 rates (2026: STANDARD NONELECTRIC $29, premium type $33) and notice (additional vehicle $11.00/night), read 2026-10-28

values.note: Senior and Access pass holders get 50% off the site they occupy (concessionaire-run).

discounts.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc/recreation/baby-doe-campground ('The Interagency Senior Pass and the Interagency Access Pass qualify for a 50% discount at concessionaire-run campsites.'), read 2026-10-28

note: USFS (Pike-San Isabel NF, Leadville Ranger District), concessionaire-run, on the east shore of Turquoise Lake at 9,900 ft, under lodgepole pine and subalpine fir. From Leadville, County Road 4 west about 3.5 miles, then County Road 9C. A boat ramp is about a mile south; the Turquoise Lake Nature Trail starts at the Molly Brown entrance. --Claude

Waterfront (stored not waterfront) - contrary claim, re-audit lead (not changed): rec.gov says 'Campsites are perched along the scenic lakeshore' and the FS 'Several popular campsites are close to the shoreline'. On imagery the premium sites (4-11, 13, 14, the $33 ones) are the row nearest the lake, ~40-100 m from the forest edge at the high-water line through lodgepole canopy (the photo shows a wide drawn-down sand band); the rest are 150 m+ back. No open apron to the water is visible - at most lakeview through trees from the premium row.

Pin 39.26972,-106.35056 is ~260 m SE of the 48 site points' centroid (39.27141,-106.35268), past the southeast end of the loops (span 426 m). Under 500 m, but the FS's own point 39.27146,-106.35246 sits at the centroid - suggest re-pinning there.

Road: PSICC's alert closes Turquoise Lake Road (County Road 4) for asphalt damage from the Abe Lee parking turnoff to Hagerman Pass; access to Turquoise Lake stays open via CR 9C and CR 9. Baby Doe's route (CR 4 from Leadville to CR 9C at the east end) should be unaffected, but the lake loop road west of Abe Lee is barricaded.
Water: FS and rec.gov both say no potable water (2025 and 2026), so potable_water is recorded false; the FS description paragraph still lists 'potable water' - restore it if service returns.
Max stay: rec.gov's 14-night rules carry 2019-2025 end dates; neither page states a current limit, so max_stay_nights left unset.
Correction: the stored note said 'Turquoise/Twin Lakes' - Baby Doe is on Turquoise Lake only.
